- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in the late part of the forecast horizon, particularly when true values show strong mean reversion or consolidation.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes; model tends to overreact and peak too high, then corrects downward.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the first 5–10 days of forecast, then gradually converges toward true mean.
- When history shows strong downward momentum, model often fails to fully reflect the trend, underestimating the drop.
- Model tends to ignore short-term volatility and overweights long-term trends, leading to lagged corrections.
- In periods of high volatility, model overfits recent highs and fails to adjust for upcoming corrections.
- When true values show a clear downward trend after a peak, model often continues to forecast upward, missing the turning point.
